newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to decide gas concession by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to decide gas concession by year-end.

text.p: Bulgaria will take a decision on a pipeline concession for transiting Russian gas through its territory by the end of the year, Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov said on Wednesday.

Bulgaria's government has opened a procedure for granting a concession to the Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company Topenergy and to set up a working group that will consider which operations and facilities to grant a concession to.

"We made our analysis, we have the opinion of a Western consultant and by the end of the year we will have a decision on the matter," Ovcharov, who heads a working group dealing with the issue, told reporters at the airport before leaving for Slovakia.
Topenergy was established in 1995 by Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and Bulgarian gas monopolist Bulgargas,
Topenergy officials said earlier this week the company needed Bulgaria's decision on a concession on the gas pipelines by February.
They said Gazprom, which holds 50 percent in the joint company, was looking at alternative plans, including building a pipeline under the Black Sea to supply Russian gas to Turkey.

Topenergy would need a concession of 30 or 50 years as enlarging the gas transit system on Bulgarian territory is expected to cost some $500 million, and would like a concession covering the whole Bulgarian network.
On Monday Topenergy invited competitive offers for planning the construction of two transit gas pipeline links to Bulgaria's Balkan neighbours Turkey and Serbia and a compressor station.
Bulgargas executive director Petar Sabev said his firm, which holds a 25.1 percent stake in Topenergy, had not been informed of the tender.
"The construction of new gas pipelines and a concession must be decided by the government. The concession issue has a political aspect," Sabev said.
Ovcharov and Sabev will pay a three-day visit to Slovakia exchanging experience related mainly to upgrading Soviet-made nuclear power stations and gas transiting.
Slovakia transits 90 billion cubic metres of Russian gas per year to Western Europe, Sabev said, adding that it had not granted a concession so far for gas transiting.
